questions.question_description: Implement Merge Sort to sort an array of integers in ascending order. You MUST print the entire array state immediately after every sub-array merge operation finishes.
questions.input_format: Integer N (size of array), followed by N space-separated integers.
questions.output_format: Print the full space-separated array on a new line after each successful `merge`.
questions.constraints: N <= 1000. Use standard integer typing. Handle an empty list without seg-faulting.
questions.hints: Divide the array into halves, sort them recursively, and merge. Print the global array at the very end of your `merge` function.
questions.solution_explanation: Merge sort guarantees O(N log N) functionality utilizing implicit tree partitioning. An extra array constructs linearly inside the merge block preventing variable overwriting during swaps.

questions.question_description: Implement Heap Sort to sort an array of integers in ascending order. You MUST print the initial fully built max heap array in one line, and then print the array state after EACH element extraction.
questions.input_format: Integer N (size of array), followed by N space-separated integers.
questions.output_format: Print the max heap structure first. Then print the array after every max element is bubbled to the end.
questions.constraints: N <= 1000. Implement exactly using an array representation heap, O(1) auxiliary space.
questions.hints: Build a Max Heap and print it. Then repeatedly extract the maximum element (root), swap it with the last element of the remaining heap, re-heapify, and PRINT the array.
questions.solution_explanation: By reorganizing parent limits recursively against child pointers inside 'heapify', the array implicitly balances like a tree. Iterating extract ops natively results in a pure completely sorted collection.

questions.question_description: Implement Quick Sort to sort an array of integers in ascending order. You MUST print the entire array state immediately after every successful partition operation.
questions.input_format: Integer N (size of array), followed by N space-separated integers.
questions.output_format: Print the full space-separated array on a new line after each `partition`.
questions.constraints: N <= 1000. The array is updated directly inline with minimal swap overhead variables.
questions.hints: Pick a pivot (last element), partition the array, and IMMEDIATELY print the global array state before recursing into the lower and upper halves.
questions.solution_explanation: Quick sort achieves outstanding functional limits sorting variables completely in-place avoiding external buffer loops. Best case runs highly optimal O(N log N) relying exactly on intelligent partition boundaries.
